## Rule

Every 9x9 input contains only background `0` and marker `5`. Each marker is at least one cell inboard. Output preserves each `5` and paints color `1` into the eight neighboring cells, leaving all other active cells as background and all canvas padding all-zero.

The live graph implements this as a single dense 3x3 Conv: identity on all channels, plus ch5 ring taps adding to ch1 and subtracting from ch0.

## Algorithm sketch

```python
out = zeros_like_30x30_onehot()
for each active cell:
    out[0, r, c] = 1
for each marker (r, c) where input[r][c] == 5:
    out[0, r, c] = 0
    out[5, r, c] = 1
    for each 8-neighbor (rr, cc):
        out[0, rr, cc] = 0
        out[1, rr, cc] = 1
```

## Cost analysis

Current cost is entirely the dense `Conv` initializer: `[10,10,3,3] = 900` params, memory 0 because the Conv output is the graph output.

The obvious sparse view has only 26 nonzero weights, but sparse initializers are not scoreable as Conv inputs under the sanitizer/ORT path. The direct #109/#119 free-output Einsum can express the rule exactly as `identity/correction + ch5 box`, but exact spatial shifts require dense row and column basis matrices, costing 3,800 params. A grouped Conv would be attractive at 180-190 params, but output ch0/ch1 would have to infer marker-neighbor rings from ch0 alone; that local classifier is not linearly separable on the generator-shaped finite patch set.

No improved candidate staged from this pass. The remaining plausible lower route would need a different primitive that inherits `input` for free and writes the ring patch with substantially fewer than the ScatterND/TopK index tax; I did not find one below 900.

| direct pool/morphology as graph output | 0 | killed by visible gate | `MaxPool` and `AveragePool` both score 0, but both visible-gate 0/265 because channel routing is wrong: marker dilation stays in ch5 or averages all channels instead of writing ch1 and preserving only center ch5 |
| groups=2 direct Conv reading ch0 for ch0/ch1 and ch5 identity for markers | about 450-460 params if feasible | killed by LP | the required ch1-vs-ch0 active decision boundary is not linearly separable from 3x3 ch0 patches; the stricter active multiclass LP with marker override is also infeasible |
| direct QLinearConv | sub-900 params in theory | invalid for this input | ONNX QLinearConv requires integer input tensors, while the task graph input is F32 |
| Cast F32 input then QLinearConv | >=9000 memory before params | over budget | full `[1,10,30,30]` U8 cast materializes 9000 charged bytes before the convolution can help |
| crop/process/pad or equal-tail/Where overlay | >=900 condition/canvas, usually >3000 for F32 crop | over budget or tie-before-work | a full bool condition is already 900B, and any F32 spatial crop of the one-hot input is larger than the live Conv params before ring construction |
| ScatterND ring patches | over budget under available index primitives | over budget | variable marker coordinates require dynamic index extraction; without a free NonZero-style source, TopK/Gather/ArgMax surfaces dominate the 900B target |

This is a formulation-relative floor for the audited sub-900 families, not an absolute source-level proof.

## 2026-06-22 floor proof (w-095): 900 is the floor; the dense Conv is optimal

Two exhaustive families, both bounded above 900:

**(A) Single-op family — floor exactly 900.** A memory-0 graph must be a single op `input[1,10,30,30] → OP → output[1,10,30,30]` (any 2nd op materialises a non-I/O intermediate that is charged). The rule is genuinely **cross-channel**: out_ch0 = id(in0) − ring(in5), out_ch1 = ring(in5), out_ch5 = id(in5) (verified from the live Conv weights: nonzero (out,in) taps are the 10 diagonal identities plus `(0,5)` and `(1,5)`). The output has 10 channels, so `out_dim = 10` is forced. The `(5→0)` and `(5→1)` taps force ch5 and ch0/ch1 into the same conv group; channels {0,1,5} are **not contiguous**, so a grouped Conv/ConvTranspose cannot place them in one contiguous group without a Transpose/Gather (an intermediate). Hence groups=1, weight `[10,10,3,3]` = **900**. ConvTranspose weight `[in,out/g,kh,kw]` = same 900. **No single op is < 900.** (Sparse Conv weights rejected by sanitizer — core.md; depthwise-only W[10,1,3,3]=90 cannot produce the ring in ch1.)

**(B) Multi-op crop family — floor ~970, measured 1162.** The only way to shrink intermediates below the 900-byte 30×30 plane is to crop to the active grid. The ARC-GEN generator (`task_4258a5f9.py`) hardcodes `size=9` with all markers inboard, so the active grid is always 9×9 (planes = 81 B U8). But two costs are structurally forced:
  - **f32 channel-slice = 324 B.** ch5 must be extracted as a small plane; `Slice(input, ch5, 0:9, 0:9)` is the only single op that crops channel+space, and it preserves the F32 input dtype → `[1,1,9,9]` F32 = 324 B (Gather can't crop spatially; casting the whole input first = 9000 B).
  - **channels-0..5 pre-pad tensor = 486 B.** The output's nonzero channels are 0,1,5; `Pad`-as-output only extends contiguously, so the pre-pad tensor must span channels 0..5 = `[1,6,9,9]` (486 B U8/BOOL). Placing ch5 content at 30×30 to use a Concat instead costs a 900-B `[1,1,30,30]` plane.
  
  324 + 486 = **810 forced**, plus ≥2 compute planes for the ring (marker-u8 + value/box ≈ 162) ⇒ **~970 floor, > 900.** The measured leanest build (`task095_crop_lean.onnx`) is **1162** (mem 1134 + params 28), fully correct (visible 265/265, truth 200000/200000, static==profile). Removing the redundant cast and using `Where(bool,u8,u8)` for `value` shaves the compute to ~3 planes (~1053) — still above 900.

**Verdict: 900 (the live dense Conv, team-best) is the absolute floor under the available primitives.** The dense `[10,10,3,3]` "wastefulness" is illusory: every alternative either (a) keeps a single 10-output Conv = 900, or (b) crops and pays an irreducible 324 (f32 slice) + 486 (channels-0..5 one-hot) + compute ≥ 970. No-candidate; do not re-attempt the crop/one-hot route below ~970.

## Don't-do log

- Do not retry sparse Conv weights unless the sanitizer changes; the probe fails before scoring/visible.
- Do not claim the #109 dissolve is automatically cheaper here. It is correct but costs 3,800 because the required shift matrices are dense.
- Do not use a grouped Conv that reads only ch0 for ch0/ch1 unless you add a new non-linear stage; one linear 3x3 threshold cannot separate ring vs non-ring background under the 9x9 marker-spacing generator.
- Do not treat parameter-free pooling as a candidate just because score_v2 is 0; visible is 0/265 for both direct MaxPool and AveragePool on this task.
- Do not re-attempt the crop-to-9x9 + small-one-hot + Pad-as-output route (#81/#67): it is fully CORRECT (265/265 visible, 200k truth) but floors at ~970 and measures 1162. The f32 channel-slice (324 B) + channels-0..5 one-hot span (486 B) are structurally forced and already exceed 900 before any compute. See 2026-06-22 floor proof.
